newsitem.title: FRANCE: BNP to bid for CIC - Le Monde.
newsitem.headline: BNP to bid for CIC - Le Monde.

text.p: France's Banque Nationale de Paris (BNP) will make an offer for regional bank group CIC, which is owned by state insurer GAN and is to be privatised by trade sale by the government, Le Monde newspaper reported.
BNP said it would not confirm, deny or make any immediate comment on the report, when contacted by Reuters.
The government is selling 67 percent of Credit Industriel et Commercial (CIC) and a tender for offers closes at 1600 GMT on Monday.
Afternoon daily Le Monde said BNP met on Friday to decide its final position and would make an offer without its partner Dresdner Bank but with the consent of the German bank.
Savings bank group Caisses d'Epargne would decide its final position on a possible offer on Monday afternoon, Le Monde said.
The finance ministry said earlier no announcement was to be expected on Monday on the outcome of the privatisation tender.
Ordinarily, tender result announcements are given on the day when the tender closes.
Societe Generale, another leading French commercial bank, has said it could be interested. Societe Generale is frequently tipped in the press as a rival contender.

Most commentary on the sell-off over the past few weeks has said suitors could find it hard to swallow the sale terms and conditions set by the government, concerning among other things in respect to CIC's insurance sale ties with GAN.
